facts.fact_text: The applicant was an active participant in the protest rallies, regularly attending the ongoing demonstrations and sit-ins at Freedom Square.
The applicant spent the night of 23 to 24 February 2008 at Freedom Square.
According to the applicant, on 24 February 2008 at around 10 a.m. he and two of his friends, A.Sis. and V.K., were driving home from the rally at Freedom Square.
According to the applicant, on 24 February 2008 at around 10 a.m. the car in which the applicant, A.Sis. and V.K. were travelling was blocked on Teryan Street in Yerevan by another car.
According to the applicant, masked gunmen emerged from the blocking car and demanded that the applicant and his friends get out of their car.
According to the applicant, he was thrown to the ground and searched but nothing was found.

According to the applicant, he and his companions A.Sis. and V.K. were forced into the blocking car and taken to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC).

According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the Principal Department for the Fight against Organised Crime of the Armenian Police (PDFOC) on 24 February 2008 at around 11.30 a.m. by operative police officers of the PDFOC.
According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the PDFOC on suspicion of carrying illegal arms and ammunition.
At 11.45 a.m. on 24 February 2008 the applicant was subjected to a search at the PDFOC by police officers in the presence of two attesting witnesses.
The record of the applicant's search at the PDFOC indicated that a spring baton had been found in the applicant's coat pocket.
The record of the applicant's search at the PDFOC indicated that the applicant had stated that the baton belonged to him and that he carried it for self-defence.
At an unspecified hour on 24 February 2008 the applicant's car was searched at the PDFOC and a Makarov-type pistol was found.
On 24 February 2008 one of the PDFOC officers addressed a report to the Head of the PDFOC.

According to the PDFOC officer's report, on 24 February 2008 at 11 a.m. an anonymous call had been made to the PDFOC stating that a Lexus-model black car was parked at the crossroads of Teryan and Koryun Streets in Yerevan and that its passengers were armed.

According to the PDFOC officer's report, an operative group of police officers of the PDFOC had immediately set off to the scene and taken into custody the Lexus-model black car and its passengers: the applicant, A.Sis. and V.K.
According to the PDFOC officer's report, a spring baton had been found when the applicant was searched.
According to the PDFOC officer's report, a Makarov-type pistol was found on searching the applicant's car.

On 25 February 2008 at 1.35 a.m. a record of the applicant's arrest was drawn up stating that the applicant was arrested on suspicion of having committed an offence under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan decided to allow the investigator's application for the applicant's detention, finding that, if the applicant remained at large, he could commit a new offence, abscond or obstruct the investigation.
On 21 April 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan allowed the investigator's application and extended the applicant's detention by two months.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan extended the applicant's detention on 21 April 2008 taking into account the nature and dangerousness of the imputed offence and the fact that the applicant, if he remained at large, could abscond, obstruct the investigation or avoid criminal responsibility and punishment.

On 8 May 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal dismissed the applicant's appeal against the detention extension, finding that the circumstances on which the applicant's detention was based persisted, since there was still a high risk that the applicant could obstruct the investigation and abscond.
On 23 May 2008 the investigator questioned police officer S.H., who was said to be on guard duty at Kentron Police Station on the night of 24 February 2008.
On 3 June 2008 the investigator questioned police officer A.H., who was said to be on guard duty at Kentron Police Station on the night of 24 February 2008.

Police officer S.H. stated that he had heard loud noises from outside Kentron Police Station, stepped outside and seen police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S. holding the applicant by his arms, trying to push him into the police station.

Police officer S.H. stated that the applicant was disobeying, showing resistance to the officers and trying to free himself, while shouting and making threats, and had eventually been pushed inside the station where he continued making threats.

Police officer A.H. stated that he had been inside Kentron Police Station and seen a person, whom he later recognised as a former minister, held by his arms by police officers K.H., E.P. and A.S., brought inside the station where he briefly threatened to have the officers' heads smashed and then calmed down and sat down.
Both police officers S.H. and A.H. stated that police officer K.H. had sat down when inside Kentron Police Station, holding his hand to his chest and saying that the applicant had punched him.
On 15 June 2008 the investigator applied to the court to have the applicant's detention extended once more, again making reference to the materials of criminal case no. 62202608.

In the application to extend the applicant's detention on 15 June 2008, the investigator added that, following a number of investigative measures, no sufficient evidence had been obtained directly implicating the applicant in the commission of the criminal act investigated in case no. 62202608.
On 18 June 2008 the applicant's criminal case was disjoined from case no. 62202608 as it was apparently ready for trial.

On 19 June 2008 the General Prosecutor's Office wrote to the investigator dealing with the applicant's case, drawing his attention to the fact that the applicant had been charged only under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The General Prosecutor's Office noted that the applicant's actions had also contained elements of an offence envisaged by Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal carrying of a cold weapon) and instructed the investigator to bring new charges.
On 20 June 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan extended the applicant's detention by 20 days, namely until 15 July 2008, on the same grounds as previously.
On 24 June 2008 the applicant lodged an appeal against the detention extension decision of 20 June 2008, raising the same arguments as previously.
On 26 June 2008 the investigator decided to bring a new charge against the applicant under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

The decision to bring a new charge under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code stated that a spring baton had been found in the applicant's coat pocket as a result of the personal search conducted upon bringing him to the police station on 24 February 2008.
On 7 July 2008 the investigation into the applicant's criminal case was completed and the case was referred to the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan for trial.

On 9 July 2008 the Criminal Court of Appeal decided to leave the applicant's appeal of 24 June 2008 without examination on the ground that the investigation had been completed and the case had been referred for trial.
On 14 July 2008 a judge of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan who had taken over the applicant's criminal case decided to set the case down for trial.
On 22 July 2008, during the first hearing, the applicant requested to be released from detention.
The applicant argued at the hearing on 22 July 2008 that his detention authorised by a court had expired on 15 July 2008.

The applicant argued at the hearing on 22 July 2008 that the judge had failed to address the issue of his detention when deciding to set the case down for trial on 14 July 2008, in violation of Articles 293 and 300 of the Armenian Code of Criminal Procedure.

On 22 July 2008 the judge took a decision stating that the question of the applicant's continued detention had been examined on 14 July 2008 when adopting the decision to set the case down for trial and it had been decided to leave the applicant's detention unchanged.

The judge stated on 22 July 2008 that as a result of a typographical error, the paragraph concerning the applicant's detention had not been reflected in the operative part of the decision of 14 July 2008, which was to be read as containing the phrase 'to leave the applicant's detention unchanged'.
At the next hearing on 28 July 2008 the judge presented the parties with the decision of 22 July 2008 and dismissed the applicant's request for release.

On 17 September 2008 another judge of the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan who had taken over the applicant's case decided to set the case down for trial and also ruled to leave the applicant's detention unchanged.

In the course of the trial the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan summoned for questioning police officers K.H., E.P., A.S., S.H. and A.H., who maintained their statements against the applicant.
After police officers S.H. and A.H. gave their testimony, the applicant requested additional time to prepare for their questioning.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request for additional time to prepare for questioning of police officers S.H. and A.H. on the ground that the applicant and his defence lawyers had had enough time to prepare themselves.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan stated that it was ready to allow a request for additional preparation time in the future if it were substantiated.
At the next court hearing the applicant lodged a similar request, seeking to summon and question police officers S.H. and A.H.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan announced that it would examine the applicant's request to summon police officers S.H. and A.H. after the applicant's questioning but it appears that it never revisited that question.
The applicant pleaded not guilty and contested the factual allegations against him at trial.
The applicant lodged several requests with the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan seeking to call witnesses on his behalf.
The applicant requested that a number of persons be summoned as witnesses, including S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y., who were his relatives, political supporters and one journalist.

The applicant submitted that S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y. had gathered at Kentron Police Station and had been standing at the entrance when he was brought back by police officers from the forensic examination and could confirm that no incident had taken place as he left the car and entered the police building.
The applicant requested that A.Sis. and V.K., who had been kept at Kentron Police Station on the night from 24 to 25 February 2008, be summoned as witnesses.

The applicant submitted that A.Sis. and V.K. had witnessed from their cell window how he had been escorted into the police building and later had heard no shouts or sounds of protest when he had been escorted through the lobby inside the building.
In support of the requests to call witnesses, the applicant's lawyer submitted records of statements which the lawyer had taken from those persons containing their relevant submissions.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request to summon S.A., V.A., L.S., P.K., K.G. and A.Y. on the ground that the case file contained no information about those persons.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan dismissed the applicant's request to summon A.Sis. and V.K. on the ground that it was not necessary to call those persons since the materials of the case contained sufficient information to draw appropriate conclusions.

The applicant's lawyer requested the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan to admit as evidence the records of the statements taken from the persons the applicant had sought to call as witnesses.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan granted the applicant's lawyer's request and the statements were included in the case file.
On 19 November 2008 the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant guilty as charged.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code to two years' imprisonment.
The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan sentenced the applicant under Article 235 § 4 of the Armenian Criminal Code to a fine in the amount of 300,000 Armenian drams (AMD).

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant had illegally carried a spring baton (mace) characterised as a striking-crushing cold weapon, which was found in his coat pocket and seized during his personal search on 24 February 2008.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant, having found out about the need to take samples from him, became agitated, started complaining and, on the way back to Kentron Police Station, made threats of retribution against the accompanying police officers who were performing their official duties.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that near the entrance to Kentron Police Station, police officer K.H. and witnesses E.P. and A.S. ordered the applicant to step out of the car and to enter the police building, and the applicant disobeyed their lawful order.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that after police officer K.H. repeated the order, the applicant first pushed and then, using non-life and health-threatening violence, pulled and punched police officer K.H. several times in the chest, causing him physical pain.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found it established that the applicant was thereafter forcibly taken inside the lobby of Kentron Police Station, while he continued his threats addressed at the police officers.

In reaching its findings, the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan relied on the statements of the police officers, the record of the applicant's bringing-in, the record of the applicant's search, the conclusions of the forensic expert characterising the baton as a striking-crushing cold weapon, and the applicant's statement of 24 February 2008 in which he had admitted that the baton belonged to him.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found the applicant's arguments and the materials submitted by him to be unreliable, in conflict with the circumstances of the case and provided by persons who had close relations with the applicant, were not impartial and aimed to protect him.
